notes: Summary: mid-market product analytics SaaS. Evaluating Hosted API first (POC) -> Dedicated for predictable unit economics. Goal: replace fragmented embedding + search infra and centralize chat support model.

Business context: customer operates multi-tenant model for 3rd-party customers; heavy compliance in finance vertical for top accounts. Wants VPC + audit logs; eventual private option considered for EU customers.
Timeline (high level):
- 2025-11-20: Intro call (AE Jordan). High level requirements — need embeddings + chat latency < 200ms p50 for support-agent flow.
- 2025-12-10: Hosted API demo (Priya led). Walked through streaming, function calling, embeddings endpoint. Feedback: SDK good, logs/observability still key.
- 2026-01-07: POC kickoff on Hosted API (2-week). Target: embed 10M docs sample, 50k queries/day sim load.
- 2026-01-21: POC mid-point. Observed token spend ~1.2M tokens/day during simulated peak, average response latency ~220ms (need squeeze). Using caching + batching recommended by Redwood Optimize.
- 2026-02-05: POC wrap + feature demo for execs. Customer asked for Dedicated for cost predictability and data isolation for finance customers.
- 2026-02-18: Pricing review call (Jordan, Priya, Liam + Cobalt procurement). Discussed commit tiers, burst, overage; recorded Fireflies ff_2026-02-18_lookback-meeting-5442.
POC learnings / technical notes:
- Workload: mixed queries — 60% embeddings/semantic search, 30% chat support (short context), 10% reranking and batch ingestion.
- Latency target: p50 < 200ms, p95 < 800ms for chat; embeddings pipeline can accept 500-1000ms p95.
- Throughput: steady 30 qps embeddings during daytime, spikes to 120 qps during batch refresh. KV caching will reduce repeating prefix costs.
Pricing/packaging discussion (current state):
- Redwood proposal v3: 12-month committed token equivalent with three commit bands: 250M, 750M, 2B tokens/month. Proposed volume discount tiers attached in drive.
- Desired by customer: start small and ramp: month1 at ~30% commit, linear ramp to 100% by month6. Wants commitment ramp schedule in contract to avoid early overage penalties.

- Burst: request for 2x burst capacity above committed baseline with guaranteed fallback to hosted variants. Customer asks for a guaranteed burst floor (e.g., 100k tokens/day) with defined billing treatment.

- Overage: customer pushes for overage capped at 1.25x list price for first 6 months, then standard 1.5x thereafter. Procurement flag: absolute cap on monthly overage exposure (limit percentage of commit).

- Ramp discount ask: 3-month ramp with partial billing at 50% of committed rate for months 1-3. Redwood counter: 6-month ramp with graded discounts (50% month1, 75% month2-3, full by month6) to protect capacity planning.
Operational & compliance asks:
- VPC peering + private endpoints: required for finance customers (must be in SOW).
- Audit logs retention: wants 7 years for top-tier customers — legal asking if Redwood can provide exportable logs; Redwood offered streaming to S3 and longer retention add-on.
- SSO/SAML + SCIM: must be available prior to go-live for staged rollout.
- Data residency: EU region pinning for a subset of customer data; currently evaluating Private deployment for EU region later in the year.
Risks / blockers we flagged:
- Procurement pushback on open-ended overage exposure (ask: hard cap per month).
- Legal wants indemnity language and stricter SLA (99.95%) than standard Redwood draft (99.9%).
- Engineering concern: p95 chat latency still slightly above target on Hosted POC; need runtime tuning (kernel selection + batching) if we move to Dedicated with tight SLOs.
